limitations: Synthetic Volcengine TTS and digital mono PCM mixing only; not human or physical microphone/AEC/playback acceptance.
Fixed corpus with repeated-speaker order and voice/name counterbalance; small number of independent sessions. No reliability percentile claimed.
Common synthetic context and denying Gateway stub. Speaker uses the pinned deployed code and matching configuration in an isolated instance, not a production customer call.
Speaker identity tracking and spoken identity answers are separate metrics. Native spoken-name binding is not an exposed stable speaker-ID or authorization signal.
Similar-voice native failure is a consistent name/preference binding reversal. Speaker merges both voices.
Embedding calibration uses the existing Speaker embedding model and is descriptive, not independent human perceptual verification. Daily pair is more separated than the obvious pair by this metric.
Current Candidate extra stop-ASR and real browser playback are not part of this native-only comparison. Passing background tests here does not establish the helper route passed.
Delivered-PCM latency is server output delivery for correct answers only; no physical speaker latency comparison.
